transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

E18 on your Bosch means the machine has detected that water is not draining within the expected time. Since there is still water in the drum, this is almost probably caused by a blockage in the drainage system rather than a major mechanical failure. The most common cause is debris (like coins, buttons, or lint) clogging the pump filter at the bottom front of the machine. Please switch off and unplug the appliance first for safety. Then open the small kick-plate flap at the bottom front, place some towels down to catch water, and slowly unscrew the drain filter. Tell me exactly what you find inside: is it clear, or are there objects blocking it?

Thanks, I've unplugged it. I had to drain the water out first using the little emergency hose, which took a while. When I unscrewed the filter there was a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it, plus a lot of fluff. I'm also a bit wet on the floor from it. What should I do next?

Good work clearing that out; finding a sock and hair grip explains why the E18 error happened. Since you drained the water manually, the machine won't run until the pump can move the remaining water freely. Please check inside the filter housing: shine a torch in and gently turn the small plastic impeller with your finger. If it spins freely, we likely just need to reset the fault; if it's still caught or stiff, that object is preventing drainage even after removing the filter.
I've turned the impeller with my finger (power still off) and it turns, slightly notchy at first and then free. What should I do now?

Since the impeller was notchy but now spins free, there may still be small debris inside the pump housing or a kink in the drain hose preventing full flow. The best way to confirm if this is fixed is to test it: screw the filter back in tightly (ensure the seal is clean), plug the machine back in, and run a 'Drain & Spin' programme. If it drains fully without showing E18 again, you're good to go; if it fails or shows E18, we'll need to check the drain hose at the back.
Ok, I've put the filter back in tightly, plugged it in and run the rinse & spin programme. It drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spun normally. Is there anything else I should do?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. To help prevent this from happening again, I recommend popping a coin or small object into the filter housing occasionally to check for debris, and always remember to remove items from pockets before washing. If you have any other questions about your appliance, just let me know.

candidates: Clogged pump filter or drain hose blockage (high)
Foreign object caught in the pump impeller (medium)
Faulty drain pump or wiring issue (low)
